title: CUET General Test Test 14
subject: General Test (Code: 501)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/General Test - 501.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: CUET (UG) 2025 and 2026 General Test shift analyses (no questions copied)

instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
The last 5 questions are a data-interpretation set based on one table; the set stays together.

questions.sub_topic: First Governor-General of Bengal
questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of Bengal, under the Regulating Act of 1773?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Warren Hastings
Why: The Regulating Act of 1773 made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal; Warren Hastings was the first to hold the post.
Why not the others: (B) was Governor of Bengal before the Act. (C) introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793). (D) became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833.
Key point: The Regulating Act also set up a Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774).

questions.sub_topic: Combining two ratios
questions.question: If a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 4 : 5, what is a : b : c?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 8 : 12 : 15
Given: b is 3 in the first ratio and 4 in the second; make both 12.
Step 1: a : b = 2 : 3 = 8 : 12; b : c = 4 : 5 = 12 : 15.
Step 2: a : b : c = 8 : 12 : 15.
Common mistake: joining the ratios without making b the same (2 : 3 : 5, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Syllogism of chairs, tables and desks
questions.question:
Statements:
All chairs are tables.
All tables are desks.
Conclusions:
I. All chairs are desks.
II. Some desks are chairs.
options: C) Both I and II follow
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Both I and II follow
Answer steps: chairs ⊂ tables ⊂ desks, so all chairs are desks (I). Since every chair is a desk, some desks are chairs (II).
Why not the others: (A) and (B) each miss one conclusion. (D) rejects both.
Key point: "All A are B" also gives "Some B are A".

questions.sub_topic: Time for a leak to empty a tank
questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 10 hours. Because of a leak at the bottom, it takes 12 hours to fill the tank. How long would the leak take to empty the full tank?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 60 hours
Given: the leak's rate = filling rate without the leak − filling rate with the leak.
Step 1: = 1/10 − 1/12 = 6/60 − 5/60 = 1/60 of the tank per hour.
Step 2: So the leak empties the tank in 60 hours.
Common mistake: subtracting the times (12 − 10 = 2 hours, option B), or adding them (22 hours, option A).

questions.sub_topic: Colour that bends most in a prism
questions.question: When white light passes through a glass prism, which colour bends the most?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Violet
Why: Violet light has the shortest wavelength of visible light and slows down most in glass, so it is bent (refracted) the most.
Why not the others: (B) bends the least. (C) and (D) bend by amounts in between.
Key point: The splitting of white light into colours is called dispersion; the order is VIBGYOR.

questions.sub_topic: Rulers of ancient India in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following rulers in chronological order (earliest first):
A. Ashoka
B. Kanishka
C. Chandragupta Maurya
D. Bindusara
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) C, D, A, B
Why: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire (c. 321 BCE); his son Bindusara followed; Ashoka, Bindusara's son, ruled c. 268–232 BCE; Kanishka of the Kushana dynasty ruled in the 1st–2nd century CE.
Why not the others: (A) puts Bindusara before his father. (B) puts Ashoka before Bindusara. (C) puts Kanishka before Ashoka.
Key point: Kanishka was a patron of Buddhism and held the Fourth Buddhist Council.

questions.sub_topic: Two rows of three facing each other
questions.question: A, B and C sit in a row facing north. D, E and F sit in another row facing south, directly opposite them. B sits in the middle of its row. E sits opposite B. A sits at the left end of its row. F sits opposite A. Who sits opposite C?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) D
Answer steps: facing north, the left end is the west end, so A is at the west end, B in the middle and C at the east end. F is opposite A (west) and E opposite B (middle), so D is opposite C (east).
Why not the others: (B) E faces B. (C) F faces A. (D) B is in the same row as C.
Key point: Fix one row first, then read the other row across from it.

questions.sub_topic: Instrument that measures electric current
questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure electric current in a circuit?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Ammeter
Why: An ammeter, connected in series in a circuit, measures current in amperes.
Why not the others: (A) measures potential difference and is connected in parallel. (C) measures distance travelled. (D) measures air pressure.
Key point: An ammeter has a very low resistance, so it hardly changes the current it measures.

questions.sub_topic: Area of the four walls of a room
questions.question: A room is 10 m long, 8 m wide and 4 m high. What is the area of its four walls?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 144 m²
Given: area of four walls = 2 × height × (length + width).
Step 1: = 2 × 4 × (10 + 8).
Step 2: = 144 m².
Common mistake: working out the volume (10 × 8 × 4 = 320, option A), or adding the floor and ceiling (144 + 80 + 80 = 304, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Word that cannot be made from TEMPERATURE
questions.question: Which of the following words cannot be formed using the letters of the word TEMPERATURE (each letter used only as often as it appears)?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) RUPTURE
Answer steps: TEMPERATURE has T ×2, E ×3, M, P, R ×2, A and U ×1. RUPTURE needs two Us, but there is only one.
Why not the others: (A) needs P, R ×2, E ×2, M, A, T, U — all available. (B) and (C) also use available letters (TREAT uses both Ts).
Key point: Count repeated letters before deciding.

questions.sub_topic: First right angle after two o'clock
questions.question: After how many minutes past 2 o'clock are the hands of a clock at right angles for the first time?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 27 3/11 minutes
Answer steps: at 2:00 the hour hand is 60° ahead. The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute and must get 90° ahead, so it must gain 60° + 90° = 150°. Time = 150 ÷ 5.5 = 27 3/11 minutes.
Why not the others: (A) is when the hands meet (a gain of 60°). (B) and (D) are not right-angle times.
Key point: For the first right angle after H o'clock, the minute hand must gain 30H + 90 degrees (when the hour hand is ahead).

questions.sub_topic: What optogenetics uses to control nerve cells
questions.question: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries on optogenetics. This technique controls the activity of nerve cells by means of:
options: D) electric shocks from implanted wires
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) light
Why: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel shared the prize for discoveries about light-gated ion channels. Nerve cells given these channels can be switched on or off with flashes of light.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are other ways of affecting the brain, but optogenetics ("opto" = light) uses light.
Key point: The light-sensitive proteins were first found in algae.

questions.sub_topic: Coding with alternate forward and backward shifts
questions.question: MANGO is coded as NZOFP. Using the same rule, what is the code for GRAPE?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) HQBOF
Answer steps: the letters move +1, −1, +1, −1, +1 in turn (M → N, A → Z, N → O, G → F, O → P). GRAPE: G → H, R → Q, A → B, P → O, E → F, giving HQBOF.
Why not the others: (B) moves every letter forward. (C) moves every letter back. (D) moves P forward instead of back.
Key point: When some letters go forward and some back, look for a pattern by position.

questions.sub_topic: Cause and effect between a price cut and demand
questions.question:
Statement I: The government reduced the price of cooking-gas cylinders.
Statement II: The demand for cooking-gas cylinders increased.
options: A) Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect
B) Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect
C) Both statements are effects of a common cause
D) Both statements are independent causes
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect
Answer steps: a lower price makes the cylinders cheaper to buy, so more people buy them. The price cut (I) leads to the rise in demand (II).
Why not the others: (B) reverses the order of events. (C) needs a third event behind both. (D) ignores the clear link.
Key point: When the price of a good falls, the demand for it usually rises.

questions.sub_topic: Assumptions behind advice to book tickets online
questions.question:
Statement: "Book your train tickets online and avoid long queues at the counter."
Assumptions:
I. Many people can use the internet to book tickets.
II. Online booking is always cheaper than counter booking.
options: B) Both I and II are implicit
C) Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Only I is implicit
Answer steps: the advice is useful only if people can book online, so I is implicit. The statement is about saving time, not money, so II is not implicit.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) accept II, which the statement does not need. (C) rejects I, without which the advice makes no sense.
Key point: An assumption is what must be true for the statement to make sense.

questions.sub_topic: Regulator of the insurance sector
questions.question: Which body regulates the insurance sector in India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) IRDAI
Why: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), set up in 1999 and based in Hyderabad, regulates insurance companies.
Why not the others: (A) regulates the stock markets. (B) regulates banks. (D) regulates pension funds, such as the National Pension System.
Key point: IRDAI was created on the recommendation of the Malhotra Committee.

questions.sub_topic: Solving a linear equation in one variable
questions.question: Find the number which, when multiplied by 5 and then reduced by 3, gives the same result as twice the number increased by 9.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 4
Given: let the number be x, so 5x − 3 = 2x + 9.
Step 1: 5x − 2x = 9 + 3, so 3x = 12.
Step 2: x = 4. (Check: 5 × 4 − 3 = 17 and 2 × 4 + 9 = 17.)
Common mistake: subtracting 3 instead of adding it (3x = 6, x = 2, option A).

questions.sub_topic: Art form of a 2026 Padma Vibhushan awardee
questions.question: N. Rajam, honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in the Padma Awards announced in January 2026, is renowned as a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Hindustani classical violinist
Why: N. Rajam is known for adapting the violin to the singing style (gayaki) of Hindustani music. She was one of five Padma Vibhushan awardees announced on 25 January 2026.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are other art forms; she is a violinist.
Key point: The Padma Vibhushan is India's second-highest civilian award, after the Bharat Ratna.

questions.sub_topic: Uncle through a mother who is an only daughter
questions.question: A's mother is the only daughter of B's father. B is a man. How is B related to A?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Uncle
Answer steps: the only daughter of B's father is B's sister. She is A's mother, so B is the brother of A's mother — A's maternal uncle.
Why not the others: (A) would be the mother's husband. (B) would share A's parents. (C) is B's father, not B.
Key point: A mother's brother is a maternal uncle.

questions.sub_topic: National tree of India
questions.question: Which is the national tree of India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Banyan
Why: The banyan (Ficus benghalensis) is the national tree. Its aerial roots grow down into new trunks, so one tree can spread over a large area.
Why not the others: (A) is valued for medicine. (B) is the tree under which the Buddha is said to have gained enlightenment. (D) is a sacred ornamental tree.
Key point: The national flower is the lotus, and the national fruit is the mango.

questions.sub_topic: Largest planet in the Solar System
questions.question: Which is the largest planet in the Solar System?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Jupiter
Why: Jupiter, a gas giant, is more than 11 times as wide as the Earth and more massive than all the other planets put together.
Why not the others: (A) is the second largest. (B) is the fourth largest. (C) is the largest of the rocky planets.
Key point: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm larger than the Earth.

questions.sub_topic: Original fraction after changes to its parts
questions.question: If the numerator of a fraction is increased by 20% and its denominator is decreased by 10%, the fraction becomes 16/21. What was the original fraction?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 4/7
Given: new fraction = original × 1.2 ÷ 0.9 = original × 4/3.
Step 1: Original × 4/3 = 16/21.
Step 2: Original = 16/21 × 3/4 = 12/21 = 4/7.
Common mistake: multiplying by 4/3 instead of dividing (giving a fraction greater than 16/21), or undoing only the change to the numerator.

questions.sub_topic: Musicians and their instruments
questions.question:
Match the musicians in List-I with their instruments in List-II:

List-I
(A) Ravi Shankar
(B) Zakir Hussain
(C) Hariprasad Chaurasia
(D) Amjad Ali Khan

List-II
(I) Tabla
(II) Sitar
(III) Sarod
(IV) Flute
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
Why: Ravi Shankar — sitar (II); Zakir Hussain — tabla (I); Hariprasad Chaurasia — bansuri flute (IV); Amjad Ali Khan — sarod (III).
Why not the others: (B) swaps Ravi Shankar and Zakir Hussain; (C) swaps Zakir Hussain and Hariprasad Chaurasia; (D) swaps Hariprasad Chaurasia and Amjad Ali Khan.
Key point: Ravi Shankar received the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

questions.sub_topic: State of the river island Majuli
questions.question: Majuli, one of the largest river islands in the world, lies in the Brahmaputra in which state?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Assam
Why: Majuli, in Assam, is a centre of the Vaishnava culture started by Srimanta Sankardeva, with many satras (monasteries). It became India's first island district in 2016.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are crossed by other large rivers but not by the Brahmaputra.
Key point: Majuli is shrinking because of erosion by the river.

questions.sub_topic: Winner of the 2026 Wimbledon men's singles
questions.question: Who won the men's singles title at Wimbledon in July 2026, beating Alexander Zverev in the final?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Jannik Sinner
Why: Jannik Sinner of Italy beat Zverev in four sets on 12 July 2026, winning Wimbledon for the second year running.
Why not the others: (C) lost to Sinner in the semi-final. (A) and (D) did not reach the final.
Key point: Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam event played on grass.

questions.sub_topic: Assertion and reason on metals and heat
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Metals such as copper are poor conductors of heat.
Reason (R): Metals have free electrons that can carry heat and electricity through them.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
Why: (A) is false: copper and other metals are good conductors of heat, which is why cooking pans are made of metal. (R) is true: their free electrons carry energy quickly through them.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) accept the false Assertion.
Key point: Silver is the best conductor of heat and electricity; copper is next.

questions.sub_topic: Mark-up needed with a free-article offer
questions.question: A shopkeeper gives one article free with every four bought, and still makes a profit of 20%. By what percentage above the cost price did he mark the articles?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 50%
Given: the customer pays the marked price of 4 articles and gets 5.
Step 1: Money received = 4 × MP; cost of 5 articles = 5 × CP. For a 20% profit: 4 MP = 1.2 × 5 CP = 6 CP.
Step 2: MP = 1.5 CP, which is 50% above cost.
Common mistake: adding the 20% discount to the 20% profit (40%, option B), or treating the offer as a 25% discount and ignoring the profit.

questions.sub_topic: Harvest festivals and their states
questions.question:
Match the harvest festivals in List-I with their states in List-II:

List-I
(A) Pongal
(B) Onam
(C) Lohri
(D) Nuakhai

List-II
(I) Odisha
(II) Punjab
(III) Kerala
(IV) Tamil Nadu
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Pongal — Tamil Nadu, in mid-January (IV); Onam — Kerala, with boat races and flower carpets (III); Lohri — Punjab, around a bonfire in January (II); Nuakhai — western Odisha, eating the new rice (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Pongal and Onam; (B) swaps Onam and Lohri; (D) swaps Lohri and Nuakhai.
Key point: Makar Sankranti is celebrated across India around the same time as Pongal and Lohri.

questions.sub_topic: Blood vessels that join arteries to veins
questions.question: Which very thin blood vessels connect the smallest arteries to the smallest veins?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Capillaries
Why: Capillaries have walls only one cell thick, so oxygen, food and wastes pass between the blood and the body's cells through them.
Why not the others: (A) carry blood away from the heart. (B) carry blood back to the heart. (D) carry lymph, not blood.
Key point: Capillaries are so narrow that red blood cells pass through them in single file.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the Moon
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Moon:
A. The Moon has almost no atmosphere.
B. The same side of the Moon always faces the Earth.
C. The Moon gives out its own light.
D. Tides in the oceans are caused mainly by the Moon's gravity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and D only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A, B and D only
Why: A, B and D are correct: the Moon takes as long to spin once as to go round the Earth, so we always see the same face.
Why not the others: C is wrong: the Moon only reflects sunlight. Options (A), (C) and (D) include C.
Key point: Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole in 2023.

questions.sub_topic: Elements in order of the number of protons
questions.question:
Arrange the following elements in increasing order of the number of protons in their atoms:
A. Carbon
B. Hydrogen
C. Oxygen
D. Helium
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) B, D, A, C
Why: Hydrogen has 1 proton, helium 2, carbon 6 and oxygen 8. The number of protons is the atomic number.
Why not the others: (B) puts helium before hydrogen. (C) puts carbon before helium. (D) puts oxygen before carbon.
Key point: Elements in the periodic table are arranged by atomic number.

questions.sub_topic: Branches of science and what they study
questions.question:
Match the branches of science in List-I with what they study in List-II:

List-I
(A) Botany
(B) Zoology
(C) Seismology
(D) Cytology

List-II
(I) Cells
(II) Earthquakes
(III) Animals
(IV) Plants
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Botany — plants (IV); zoology — animals (III); seismology — earthquakes (II); cytology — cells (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps botany and zoology; (B) swaps zoology and seismology; (C) swaps seismology and cytology.
Key point: "Cyto-" means cell, as in cytoplasm.

questions.sub_topic: Number grid with a product rule
questions.question:
In each row, the third number is found from the first two by the same rule:
3, 5, 12
4, 6, 20
7, 2, ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 7
Answer steps: third = first × second − first: 3 × 5 − 3 = 12; 4 × 6 − 4 = 20. So 7 × 2 − 7 = 7.
Why not the others: (A) is only the product. (C) is the sum. (D) is the difference.
Key point: Test the rule on every row before applying it.

questions.sub_topic: Value of a machine after depreciation
questions.question: A machine worth ₹50,000 loses 10% of its value every year. What will it be worth after 2 years?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) ₹40,500
Given: each year the value is multiplied by 0.9.
Step 1: After 1 year: 50,000 × 0.9 = ₹45,000.
Step 2: After 2 years: 45,000 × 0.9 = ₹40,500.
Common mistake: subtracting 10% of the original value twice (₹40,000, option A), or stopping after one year (₹45,000, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the 2026 Chemistry Nobel
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
A. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was shared by Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai.
B. Their work concerned molecules that exist in two mirror-image forms.
C. The prize was announced in October 2026.
D. The Chemistry prize is awarded by the Norwegian Nobel Committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) B, C and D only
C) A, B, C and D
D) A, B and C only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) A, B and C only
Why: A, B and C are correct: the prize, announced on 7 October 2026, was for discovering non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric synthesis — how one mirror-image form of a molecule can come to dominate.
Why not the others: D is wrong: the Chemistry prize is awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm. Options (B) and (C) include D; (A) leaves out the correct statement C.
Key point: Living things use only one mirror-image form of their amino acids and sugars.

questions.sub_topic: Probability of drawing a face card
questions.question: One card is picked at random from a full pack of 52. Find the chance that it shows a king, a queen or a jack.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 3/13
Given: each of the 4 suits has 3 face cards, so there are 12 face cards.
Step 1: Probability = 12/52.
Step 2: = 3/13.
Common mistake: counting only the kings (4/52 = 1/13, option A), counting the aces as face cards too (16/52 = 4/13, option B), or giving the chance of one suit (1/4, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Remainder on a factor of the divisor
questions.question: A number leaves a remainder of 19 when divided by 36. What remainder will it leave when divided by 12?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 7
Given: the number = 36k + 19, and 36k is a multiple of 12.
Step 1: So the remainder depends only on 19 ÷ 12.
Step 2: 19 = 12 + 7, so the remainder is 7.
Common mistake: giving 19, which is larger than the divisor 12 and so cannot be a remainder (option B).

questions.sub_topic: Odd one out among musical instruments
questions.question: Three of these instruments belong to one family. Which one does not?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Flute
Answer steps: the violin, sitar and guitar are string instruments; the flute is a wind instrument.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) all make sound with vibrating strings.
Key point: The shehnai, like the flute, is a wind instrument.

questions.sub_topic: Assertion and reason on 2 being prime
questions.question:
Assertion (A): 2 is a prime number.
Reason (R): 2 is an even number.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Answer steps: both are true, but being even does not make a number prime — 4, 6 and 8 are even and not prime. 2 is prime because its only factors are 1 and 2. So (R) does not explain (A).
Why not the others: (A) treats evenness as the reason. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: 2 is the only even prime number.

questions.sub_topic: Number on top of a die
questions.question: The faces of a die are numbered 1 to 6 so that the numbers on opposite faces add up to 7. If 2 is on the bottom face, which number is on the top face?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 5
Answer steps: the top face is opposite the bottom face, so top = 7 − 2 = 5.
Why not the others: (A) is the bottom face itself. (C) and (D) are side faces.
Key point: On a standard die, 1–6, 2–5 and 3–4 are opposite pairs.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about ordinances
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about ordinances in India:
A. The President can issue an ordinance when Parliament is not in session.
B. An ordinance lapses six weeks after Parliament reassembles unless approved.
C. The President can amend the Constitution by an ordinance.
D. A Governor has a similar power to issue ordinances for a state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and D only
C) A, B, C and D
D) B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A, B and D only
Why: A, B and D are correct (Articles 123 and 213).
Why not the others: C is wrong: the Constitution can be amended only by Parliament under Article 368, not by an ordinance. Options (C) and (D) include C; (A) leaves out the correct statement D.
Key point: An ordinance has the same force as an Act of Parliament while it lasts.

questions.sub_topic: State with India's largest tiger reserve
questions.question: India's largest tiger reserve by area, Nagarjunsagar–Srisailam, lies mainly in which state?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Andhra Pradesh
Why: The Nagarjunsagar–Srisailam Tiger Reserve, along the Krishna river in the Nallamala hills, lies mainly in Andhra Pradesh. It is named after two dams on the river.
Why not the others: (A) has Bandipur and Nagarhole. (B) has Amrabad and Kawal. (D) has Namdapha and Pakke.
Key point: Project Tiger began with nine reserves; India now has more than 50.

questions.sub_topic: Squares minus one in falling order
questions.question: Which number comes next: 120, 99, 80, 63, 48, ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 35
Answer steps: the terms are 11² − 1, 10² − 1, 9² − 1, 8² − 1, 7² − 1, so the next is 6² − 1 = 35. (The differences 21, 19, 17, 15 also lead to 13.)
Why not the others: (A) subtracts 15 again. (B) is 6² without subtracting 1. (D) subtracts 11.
Key point: Numbers just below perfect squares are worth checking in a series.

questions.sub_topic: Minutes a train stops each hour
questions.question: Without stops, a train runs at 60 km/h; including stops, its average speed is 45 km/h. For how many minutes does the train stop in each hour?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 15 minutes
Given: because of the stops, the train covers 15 km less in each hour.
Step 1: At 60 km/h, 15 km takes 15 ÷ 60 hours.
Step 2: = ¼ hour = 15 minutes.
Common mistake: dividing 15 km by the slower speed (15 ÷ 45 hours = 20 minutes, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Homeland of the 2026 Peace laureate
questions.question: Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in October 2026, is a former UN High Commissioner for Human Rights from which country?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) South Africa
Why: Navi Pillay, a South African jurist, was honoured for her work for peace and international law. She is the first South African woman to win the prize.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are other countries with large communities of Indian origin.
Key point: The Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo by the Norwegian Nobel Committee.

questions.sub_topic: Department with the most patients over three months
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Patients treated in a hospital, by department, January to March

| Department | January | February | March |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cardiology | 120 | 140 | 160 |
| Orthopaedics | 90 | 100 | 110 |
| Paediatrics | 150 | 130 | 170 |
| Neurology | 60 | 70 | 80 |
| ENT | 80 | 60 | 80 |

Question: Which department treated the most patients over the three months taken together?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Paediatrics
Given: three-month totals — Cardiology 420, Orthopaedics 300, Paediatrics 450, Neurology 210, ENT 220.
Step 1: Compare the totals.
Step 2: Paediatrics, with 450, is the highest.
Common mistake: choosing Cardiology because it rose every month (option A); its total is only 420.

questions.sub_topic: Cardiology's share of March patients
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Patients treated in a hospital, by department, January to March

| Department | January | February | March |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cardiology | 120 | 140 | 160 |
| Orthopaedics | 90 | 100 | 110 |
| Paediatrics | 150 | 130 | 170 |
| Neurology | 60 | 70 | 80 |
| ENT | 80 | 60 | 80 |

Question: What percentage of all the patients treated in March were in Cardiology?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 26⅔%
Given: March total = 160 + 110 + 170 + 80 + 80 = 600; Cardiology in March = 160.
Step 1: Share = 160 ÷ 600.
Step 2: = 26⅔%.
Common mistake: dividing by the January or February total of 500 (32%, option A), or by Cardiology's own three-month total (160 ÷ 420 ≈ 38.1%, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Average monthly patients in Neurology
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Patients treated in a hospital, by department, January to March

| Department | January | February | March |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cardiology | 120 | 140 | 160 |
| Orthopaedics | 90 | 100 | 110 |
| Paediatrics | 150 | 130 | 170 |
| Neurology | 60 | 70 | 80 |
| ENT | 80 | 60 | 80 |

Question: What was the average number of Neurology patients per month?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 70
Given: Neurology: 60, 70, 80.
Step 1: Total = 210.
Step 2: Average = 210 ÷ 3 = 70.
Common mistake: dividing by 2 (105, option C), or giving the March or January figure (options B and D).

questions.question:

| Cardiology | 120 | 140 | 160 |
| Orthopaedics | 90 | 100 | 110 |
| Paediatrics | 150 | 130 | 170 |
| Neurology | 60 | 70 | 80 |
| ENT | 80 | 60 | 80 |

Question: What is the ratio of the total number of ENT patients to the total number of Orthopaedics patients over the three months?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 11 : 15
Given: ENT total = 80 + 60 + 80 = 220; Orthopaedics total = 90 + 100 + 110 = 300.
Step 1: 220 : 300.
Step 2: Divide by 20: 11 : 15.
Common mistake: writing the ratio the wrong way round (option A).

questions.sub_topic: Cardiology patients in April from a share
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Patients treated in a hospital, by department, January to March

| Department | January | February | March |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cardiology | 120 | 140 | 160 |
| Orthopaedics | 90 | 100 | 110 |
| Paediatrics | 150 | 130 | 170 |
| Neurology | 60 | 70 | 80 |
| ENT | 80 | 60 | 80 |

Question: In April the hospital treated 20% more patients in all than in March, and Cardiology accounted for 25% of April's patients. How many Cardiology patients were treated in April?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 180
Given: March total = 600.
Step 1: April total = 600 × 1.2 = 720.
Step 2: Cardiology in April = 25% of 720 = 180.
Common mistake: raising March's Cardiology figure by 20% (192, option A), or taking 25% of the March total (150, option C).
